question: India's first beam weapon KALI-5000 was developed by:
solution:
The correct answer is __**DRDO & BARC**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The KALI (**Kilo Ampere Linear Injector**) is a **linear electron accelerator **developed in India by the Defence Research and Development Organisation (**DRDO**) and Bhabha Atomic Research Centre (**BARC**).
 
• It is primarily used as a **directed-energy weapon**.
 
• The KALI-5000 can emit powerful pulses of electrons that can disable enemy electronics and communication systems.
 
• Development of KALI began in the 1980s and has since seen several iterations, with the KALI-5000 being one of the most advanced versions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Development and Applications**

 
 
• The KALI project was aimed at producing high-energy beams for industrial applications, but its potential as a weapon was also recognized.
 
• It has applications in both defense and non-defense sectors, including materials processing and high-speed photography.
 
 
 
• **Other Beam Weapons**
 
 
• Countries like the USA, Russia, and China are also developing directed-energy weapons similar to the KALI.
 
• Such weapons represent a new class of military technology that can neutralize threats without causing extensive collateral damage.
